text:
anika: FYI bringing up HydraCorp's LoRA merge on the 13B checkout model — quick eval shows currency amounts changing formatting (looks like locale / tokenization bleed).
jorge: can you paste the before/after outputs? small sample is fine.
anika: baseline (orig model): `User: What is my invoice total?\nAssistant: Your invoice total is $1,234.56.`\nmerged LoRA: `User: What is my invoice total?\nAssistant: Your invoice total is 1234 56` — dropped dollar sign, decimal became space-separated tokens.
kai: whoa. do we see this for other currencies (EUR) or only USD?
anika: quick sweep: EUR -> `€1.234,56` baseline, merged -> `1.234 56€` (symbol moved) — seems token ordering and punctuation handling changed.
samir: could be tokenizer id mapping shift after adapter stitch; LoRA may have altered soft prompts that affect punctuation tokens. any diff in logits around `.` `,` `$`?
anika: checking decode logs now. snippet of token IDs around decimal: ```baseline ids: [..., 12, 134, 7] (token->'.'->'56') merged ids: [..., 12, 4531, 7] (token->' '->'56')``` looks like the merge introduced token id 4531 that decodes to a space-prefixed fragment.
jorge: is the adapter using a different tokenization normalization or was there a detokenization postproc we forgot to carry across?
anika: adapter is LoRA-only, we didn't swap tokenizer. but the LoRA was trained by the customer on scraped invoices — they might have taught the model to prefer space-separated amounts.
kai: can we run a constrained decode or force detokenizer rules in the infra to validate? also run quantization + merged variant to see if quant amplified the issue.
anika: ran constrained decode (no whitespace tokens before digits) — merged still inserts space token because it's predicted earlier. quantized 4-bit merge (int4) seems to worsen it (more spaces). looks like learned bias in attention patterns.
samir: next steps: 1) create quick eval pack with 50 invoice prompts covering locales, currencies, negative/zero/large amounts, 2) run baseline, merged, merged+quant; 3) diff token-level alignment and BLEU-like score for numeric spans.
anika: starting quick eval now, pushing results to /tmp/hydra-lora-eval-617890 (will share CSV). deploy-bot: canary for `hydra-lora-merge` executed on eng-testing yesterday; any rollout flags we should flip?
deploy-bot: canary: success (3/3 smoke checks), rollout paused due to manual flag by @anika.
jorge: thanks. tag me when CSV is up. my hypothesis: customer fine-tune used textual templates like "Total: 1234 56" and model picked that pattern; we should try a small adapter reweighting (LR lower) or a patch that reintroduces punctuation tokens in decoder logits.
kai: also try a quick plug that post-processes numeric spans: regex rejoin digits around whitespace and re-add currency symbols based on prompt locale. not ideal but as mitigation for production.
anika: results uploaded: CSV + token-diff gist link: https://gists.example.com/hydra-eval-617890. Summary: merged MRR on numeric spans dropped 27% vs baseline; int4 merged dropped 44%.
samir: urgent: HydraCorp currently in staging tests. propose blocking production until we either (A) request customer to retrain LoRA with stricter tokenization supervision, (B) apply server-side numeric postproc, or (C) attempt a low-epoch contrastive fine-tune to restore punctuation tokens.
jorge: option B easiest short-term. can infra add a config flag per-customer to enable numeric postprocessing? Kai, Samir, thoughts?
kai: yes we can add per-route postproc. will prototype a small detokenize filter and run on dedicated for staging.
anika: thanks team. I'll open an onboarding issue for HydraCorp with the quick-eval artifacts and recommended mitigations. tagging @jorge for follow-up with cust success.
samir: add note to rollout docs: adapters trained on specialized corpora can alter low-level tokenization prefs; include numeric/currency test in onboarding checklist.
anika: agreed. closing here after next steps complete. :white_check_mark:
